parsed_blocks.text: On Friday Maya wants to eat out with her friend Tom. In the morning she calls a small restaurant near her house. She asks them to book a table for two people at seven.
They arrive on time. A waiter meets them at the door and shows them a table by the window. He gives them the menu and a glass of water.
Maya opens the menu and reads it slowly. The starters are on the first page: small dishes for the beginning. Then come the main courses, the big dishes in the middle. The desserts are at the end.
Next to the chicken she sees rice and salad. Rice is not a whole meal. It is a side dish, and it comes with the main course.
At the top of the menu there is one dish in a box. It is the daily special, and the cook makes it only today.

Tom does not know what to choose. He asks the waiter to recommend something. The waiter says the soup is very good today. Tom is allergic to fish, so he asks about the soup first. There is no fish in it.
Now they are ready to order. Maya says she would like the daily special. Tom orders the soup and then the chicken with rice. The waiter writes the order down and takes the menu away.
The food comes ten minutes later. They eat slowly and talk about their week. For dessert they both take ice cream.
At the end of the meal Maya asks the waiter for the bill. He brings it on a small plate. It is forty euros for the two of them. They split the bill, so each friend pays twenty euros.
Tom has no cash in his pocket today. He asks if he can pay by card. Maya pays her half in cash. Before they leave, she puts a small tip on the table for the kind waiter.

data.definition: the list of all the food and drinks that a restaurant can give you
data.example: The waiter gives them the menu and a glass of water.

data.definition: the small dish that you eat before the main course; in American English people often say appetizer
data.example: Tom takes the soup as his starter.

data.definition: the big dish in the middle of a meal, after the starter and before the dessert
data.example: Tom's main course is chicken with rice.

data.definition: the sweet dish at the end of a meal, like ice cream or fruit
data.example: For dessert they both take ice cream.

data.definition: a small plate of food, like rice or salad, that comes with the main course; people often say just a side
data.example: The rice next to the chicken is a side dish.

data.definition: the dish that a restaurant cooks for one day only, so it is different tomorrow
data.example: Maya says she would like the daily special.

data.definition: to call or write to a restaurant and ask them to keep a table free for you
data.example: In the morning she calls the restaurant to book a table.

data.definition: the person in a restaurant who takes your order and brings your food to the table; in American English people often say server
data.example: A waiter meets them at the door.

data.definition: to tell the waiter what food or drink you want; also the food you asked for
data.example: Tom orders the soup and then the chicken with rice.

data.definition: to tell someone which thing you think is good, so they can choose it
data.example: He asks the waiter to recommend something.

data.definition: made ill by one kind of food, so you must not eat it
data.example: Tom is allergic to fish, so he asks about the soup first.

data.definition: the paper that shows how much you must pay for your meal; in American English people often say check
data.example: At the end of the meal Maya asks the waiter for the bill.

data.definition: extra money that you leave for the waiter because the service is good
data.example: She puts a small tip on the table.

data.definition: to pay for a meal together, with each person paying part of it
data.example: They split the bill, so each friend pays twenty euros.

data.definition: paper money and coins that you can hold in your hand, not a card
data.example: Maya pays her half in cash.

data.definition: to pay with a bank card instead of paper money and coins
data.example: Tom has no cash, so he asks if he can pay by card.
